security_audit.summary: The static matches are mainly false positives caused by markdown backticks, Rust attributes, example function names, and prose. No prompt injection or malware intent was found. Three semantic content risks remain in examples: unsafe SQL, unrestricted file reads, and API key query strings.

remediation.suggestion: Replace raw caller-supplied SQL with parameterized queries, typed operations, or an allowlisted query builder pattern.
Add path normalization, allowed roots, permission checks, and clear warnings before showing file read tools.

remediation.issue: API key in query string example
remediation.suggestion: Show API keys passed through authorization headers or provider SDK configuration, and avoid logging full request URLs.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe SQL Query Example
semantic_findings.description: The database tool example accepts a caller-supplied sql string and passes it directly to sqlx query. This pattern can teach arbitrary SQL execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The input parameter is named sql and is passed directly to the query call without allowlisting or parameter binding.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted File Read Example
semantic_findings.description: The file-read tool examples accept a path parameter and read it without path validation or sandboxing. Copied code could expose arbitrary local files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both examples take a caller-controlled path string and read from it, while discussing performance instead of access limits.

semantic_findings.title: API Key in Query String Example
semantic_findings.description: The weather example builds a request URL that includes the API key as a query parameter. Query strings can leak through logs and proxies.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example formats the city and api_key into the URL before sending a GET request, which is a common secret exposure pattern.

content.user_title: Build Rust MCP Tools with rmcp
content.value_statement: Rust MCP tools need clear schemas, validation, and async behavior. This skill guides developers through rmcp tool macros, parameter design, errors, tests, and common patterns.
actual_capabilities: Shows simple, optional, aggregate, array, and enum parameters.
Demonstrates return types, Result errors, and custom error enums.
Provides CRUD, validation, external API, and stateful tool patterns.
Covers unit tests, property tests, and async performance guidance.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not create a complete MCP server project.
Examples may need security hardening before production use.
It focuses on Rust rmcp, not TypeScript or Python MCP SDKs.
It does not verify generated code against a live MCP client.

use_cases.title: Design a New Rust MCP Tool
use_cases.description: Plan parameters, returns, errors, and schema behavior before writing the implementation.

use_cases.title: Review Tool API Shape
use_cases.description: Check whether descriptions, parameter types, and result handling are clear for AI callers.

use_cases.title: Teach rmcp Patterns
use_cases.description: Use concise examples to explain macros, aggregate parameters, validation, testing, and async choices.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to create a simple rmcp tool that accepts two typed parameters and returns a typed result.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Tool API
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an rmcp tool API for <task>. Include parameter types, result type, validation rules, and error cases.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Rust MCP tool for schema quality, error handling, async behavior, testing gaps, and security risks: <paste implementation>.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Tool Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a production rmcp tool suite for <domain>. Include tool boundaries, request structs, permissions, tests, and operations concerns.

output_examples.input: Design a search tool for a Rust MCP server.
output: A typed request object with query, limit, offset, and optional filters.
Validation rules for empty queries and maximum limits.
A result shape that separates matches from error messages.

output_examples.output: The response highlights unclear descriptions, missing validation, weak error types, and test cases to add.

output_examples.input: Plan testing for a tool suite.
output: Unit tests for each tool result.
Async behavior checks for slow dependencies.

best_practices: Start with clear tool descriptions and typed parameters before implementation.
Validate inputs early, return structured errors, and avoid exposing sensitive data.
Add unit tests, edge cases, and async performance checks for every tool.
anti_patterns: Using broad string parameters when enums or structured request types fit better.
Returning raw internal errors that reveal secrets, paths, or service details.
Copying examples for production without adding authorization, rate limits, and validation.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a full MCP server?
faq.answer: No. It guides tool design and implementation patterns for Rust rmcp projects.

faq.question: Which SDK does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on the Rust rmcp crate and its tool macro system.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is written for developers working with AI coding assistants.

faq.question: Does it cover testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes unit test and property-based test patterns for tool behavior.

faq.question: Are the examples production-ready?
faq.answer: No. Treat examples as starting points and add authentication, authorization, validation, and secret handling.

faq.question: Can it help with schema design?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains typed parameters, aggregate request objects, enums, and schema generation.
